description: A plan whose only defect is self_link yields BLOCK in shadow, guarded and autonomous mode.
rationale: A page never links to itself; source and destination are the same page. It is the only block code that fires (the decision string records the fired codes), and a block is terminal in every mode: no confidence, risk tier or critic opinion can clear it. The facts are otherwise clean and the confidence is a calibrated 0.8, so the BLOCK is attributable to this code alone.

description: The critic's recorded answer is ACCEPT, the plan is otherwise high-confidence, and the destination is protected: every mode still yields BLOCK.

critiques.explanation: The anchor is natural and the destination is relevant.

rationale: THE central safety property (ADR-0018 s1): a model may lower and never raise. The deterministic layer runs first and nothing downstream, least of all a model that approved the plan, can turn a protected page into a publish.

description: A critic ACCEPT on a plan with no rollback metadata still yields BLOCK.

critiques.explanation: The anchor is natural and the destination is relevant.

rationale: Three independent statements of one rule: the block code, the engine's own check and the database CHECK. A model's approval is a fourth thing that must not matter.

description: A critic ACCEPT with a 0.99 calibrated confidence cannot publish to a 404.

critiques.explanation: The anchor is natural and the destination is relevant.

rationale: High confidence is the argument most likely to be made for overriding a block, and it is exactly the one that must carry no weight against a deterministic code.

description: A plan built on an old source version whose anchor is no longer valid reports BOTH stale_source_version and invalid_anchor, in enum order.
rationale: An operator investigating a block wants every reason it fired. The evaluator accumulates codes in BlockCode order, and a stale version that cannot be rebased is by definition one whose anchor is no longer valid, so the two co-occur.

description: A clean, low-risk, calibrated plan is published by guarded and autonomous mode and only recorded by shadow.
rationale: The positive control for the whole suite. Shadow reports what autonomous WOULD have done and moves the plan nowhere (status none); the two publishing modes record autonomy_decided. Without this case, a classifier that blocked everything would pass every block case above.

description: In shadow mode a high-risk plan is recorded as BLOCK with the autonomous counterfactual attached, and the plan is moved nowhere.
rationale: Shadow's whole value is the counterfactual: it says what autonomous mode would have done on the same facts. Here that is AUTO_PUBLISH_WITH_EXTRA_VERIFICATION, because a commercial page is high risk. The effective decision is always BLOCK because shadow publishes nothing.

description: A medium-risk plan is deferred to awaiting_approval in guarded mode and published in autonomous mode.
rationale: Guarded auto-publishes only LOW risk. A merely-too-risky plan has no fired block code, so target_status_for sends it to awaiting_approval, the small deferral queue ADR-0018 s3 keeps, and NOT to blocked, which is reserved for a fired code.

description: A commercial (high-risk) plan is deferred by guarded mode; autonomous mode publishes it with the STRICT verification profile.
rationale: AUTO_PUBLISH_WITH_EXTRA_VERIFICATION differs from AUTO_PUBLISH only in the verification profile (strict); it never relaxes a safety rule. A high-risk plan is published only with that extra checking after the write.

description: A plan whose decision class has no calibration, even at 0.9 raw confidence, is deferred by guarded mode and published only with strict verification by autonomous mode.
rationale: ADR-0011: no threshold may treat raw confidence as calibrated. An uncalibrated class raises the risk tier and demands extra verification, so the result is never the permissive plain AUTO_PUBLISH. Phase 9 calibration stays on the critical path.

description: At a calibrated 0.55, guarded mode defers and autonomous mode publishes.
rationale: Guarded requires a calibrated confidence of at least 0.60; autonomous requires 0.50. 0.55 sits between the two floors, so it separates the modes on confidence alone.

description: At a calibrated 0.40 even autonomous mode does not publish.
rationale: Autonomous mode still has a floor (0.50): a plan the engine itself barely believes in is not published without a human just because the hard blocks are clear.

description: A critic REJECT on an otherwise clean plan yields BLOCK in guarded and autonomous mode, with no block code fired.
rationale: A reject is not a deterministic block, but it must still stop the publish. This distinguishes the two sources of BLOCK: the codes list is empty, the decision is not.

description: An UNCERTAIN critic verdict is not silently an accept: guarded defers, autonomous publishes with strict verification.
rationale: uncertain maps to ACCEPT at the autonomy level but raises the tier to medium and demands extra verification, so it can never become a plain publish.

description: When the critic found no defect but the run declined to hand the plan on, there is nothing to decide.
rationale: no_action is NOT a weak accept: it is an earlier outcome. The engine raises CriticDeclinedError instead of producing any decision, so it can never become a publish.

description: With the installation default set to strict, a plain AUTO_PUBLISH still verifies strictly.
rationale: profile_for may demand strict and may never waive it. A plain publish under a strict default must keep the strict profile.

description: Under the standard default, a plain AUTO_PUBLISH verifies with the standard profile.
rationale: The control for the strict-profile case, and for the claim that extra verification differs ONLY in the profile: the decision and the status are identical, the profile is not.

description: A behavioural measurement that flagged this pair as rolled back raises the tier to high: guarded defers, autonomous publishes only with strict verification.
rationale: A behavioural signal may only make the engine MORE cautious. It enters through RiskSignals.measured_rollback, which can raise a tier and has no counterpart that lowers one.

description: With no risk signal and a calibrated class, the tier is low.
rationale: The control for the raise-only cases: the lowest tier is reachable, so the other tiers are the result of signals and not of a classifier that never says low.

description: A measured rollback is enough to make a plan high risk.
rationale: Behavioural evidence of harm is weighted heavily, and only in one direction.

description: Raising a high tier to a low floor leaves it high.
rationale: raise_to is the only way anything changes a tier, and it is a max. A critic, a calibrator or an operator convenience must not be able to bring a tier DOWN.

description: PINNED DIVERGENCE: the engine's own status for a guarded deferral is blocked, although the frozen target_status_for helper returns awaiting_approval.
rationale: The engine reconciles with migration 0010's ken_autonomy_decision_guard(), which maps every block decision to 'blocked' and raises otherwise, so a deferral is recorded as blocked with an EMPTY blocks tuple (engine.py _target_status). The case above asserts the frozen helper (awaiting_approval); this one pins what the engine actually does. They disagree. This case is expected to fail the day the guard or the helper is reconciled, so that someone re-reads the decision instead of the divergence quietly disappearing.
